By declaring a vacancy in the imamate, the king of Thýven could justify legally seizing the territory under former sal-baliz control and maintaining full autocractic power over the lands (since the constitution of Thýven had no dealings regarding foreign territory that was under occupation). Erjk Drs, while a careful monarch, was also a stabilising force, and a near obsessive compulsive individual. Thus when the idea of Uḍūl al-Imāmah was floated before him, he grabbed the chance to further advance Thýven's position in THEP and on the world stage. It was under this, that Erjk would justify the movement of a further 450,000 troops into the southern portion of Sal-Baliz's former territory, and it was further under this that these troops, led by general Consantin Elmorjjen would formally declare the southern region to be under "protectorate" status of Thýven.

[spoiler=[b]Treaty of Friendship, Cooperation and Trade between the Federal Republic of Hatorre and the Democratic Republic of Mosqueda[/b]

Tratado de Amistad, Cooperación y Comercio entre la República Federal de Hatorre y la República Democrática de Mosqueda]
The Federal Republic of Hatorre and the Democratic Republic of Mosqueda are signing the following Trade, Friendship, and Cooperation Agreement between Hatorre and Mosqueda.

SECTION 1. FRIENDSHIP AGREEMENT
1. From this moment on, Hatorre and Mosqueda are friendly, sister nations and will establish full diplomatic relations, with respective ambassadors in Thiollier and Manzanilla.
2. Hatorre and Mosqueda sign a Non-Aggression Pact, by which the parties agree not to attack each other in future conflicts, which may be resolved through diplomatic channels. The Non-Aggression Pact is indissoluble, and a breach of the pact will be considered when one of the parties is deemed to be violating the sovereignty of the other through military occupation.
3. Hatorre and Mosqueda will sign a Defensive Agreement, in which the militaries of the two nations will cooperate in matters of defense and security, and, if necessary, support in times of conflict. Compliance with the requests of one party to the Defensive Agreement will be freely executed by the other party.
4. The Federal Republic of Hatorre recognizes the Democratic Republic of Mosqueda as a sovereign state, and the Democratic Republic of Mosqueda recognizes the Federal Republic of Hatorre as a sovereign state, as well as their respective territorial integrity, and they undertake to respect international law.

SECTION 2. COOPERATION AGREEMENT.
1. Hatorre and Mosqueda will cooperate in matters of education, health, security, economy, and trade, ensuring that the governments of both countries pursue common goals.
2. Hatorre and Mosqueda will allow visa-free travel for their citizens between the two countries, with only a passport required.
3. Hatorre and Mosqueda will allow ships from both countries to freely dock in their ports and waters.
4. Hatorre and Mosqueda will belong to the Conference of Vespurian States, a new political organization to ensure intercontinental dialogue and cooperation between countries.

SECTION 3. TRADE AGREEMENT
1. Hatorre will have priority import rights in Mosqueda, and Mosqueda will have priority import rights in Hatorre.
2. Hatorre will sell to the Democratic Republic of Mosqueda, for a renewable period of six months, 1.24 billion barrels of crude oil at a price of US$61.75 billion.
3. Hatorre will sell to the Democratic Republic of Mosqueda, for a renewable period of one year, 20 tons of refined gold at a price of US$3,050 per ounce, for a total of US$2.15 billion.
4. Hatorre will sell to the Democratic Republic of Mosqueda, USD 3 billion in agricultural production each year, including rice, wheat, barley, onions, tomatoes, beans, turkey, strawberries and pumpkins.
5. Mosqueda will sell to the Federal Republic of Hatorre, USD 600 million in agricultural production each year, including seafood and their derivated products.

SECTION 4. INVESTMENT AGREEMENT
1. Hatorre will invest in the construction of a new commercial port in the city of São Canejas, with an investment of USD 3 billion, 10% of which will go to the Mosquedan Treasury. This new port, whose concession will be called Canejas Agrícola, will be managed by a Hatorrean holding company, and the fiscal policy with Mosqueda will be followed, with Mosqueda receiving 10% of the royalties from the profits. In 25 years, Mosquera will have 45% control of the port concession.
2. Hatorre will invest in the creation and operation of eleven mines in Mosquedan territory, under the control of six Hatorrean companies. These mines will be located in the west and east of Mosqueda. In the east, the mines will be dedicated to copper mining, and in the west, to iron mining. The investment in these mines is US$20 billion, 9% of which will go to the Mosquedan Treasury. These eleven mines will report their taxes according to Mosqueda's fiscal policy, and 6% of the profit royalties will be given to Mosqueda. In 20 years, Mosqueda will have 75% control of the eastern mines and 30% of the western mines.
3. Hatorre will respect local Mosqueda laws regarding tax and business policy, as well as the labor code.
4. Hatorre will ensure that the vast majority of employees in these investments are citizens of the Democratic Republic of Mosqueda.
7. Hatorre will be attentive to any concerns that Mosqueda may have as a result of the investments and will ensure compliance with and protection of the investments.

SECTION 5. FINAL PROVISIONS.
1. This treaty is indissoluble for all parties, unless both parties decide to dissolve it.
2. This treaty shall be the basis for any future diplomatic agreements between Mosqueda and Hatorre.

Signed,

[b]SEBASTIÁN ESPINOSA DE LOS MONTEROS[/b], President of the Federal Republic of Hatorre
[b]THE LEADER[/b], of Mosqueda[/spoiler]
